$comment: Foreground/background token pairs rated by scripts/check-contrast.mjs (WCAG 2.1). kind: text >= 4.5, large >= 3 (24px, or 18.66px bold), ui >= 3 (focus rings, borders, icons that carry state). tokens.file is the one token source; tokens.themes maps each theme to the CSS blocks read for it, in order, later blocks overriding earlier ones (a block inside an at-rule is named by its path, e.g. "@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root"); two themes may not read the same blocks, and a block no theme reads may not define a token the pairs use. Nested style rules are refused. A translucent bg needs "over", the opaque token it sits on; a translucent fg is composited onto the bg. "gate": false keeps a pair's reading in the output without failing the run; it needs a "why" citing an issue (#n), every theme keeps at least one gated pair, and an exempt pair that meets its threshold fails the run until the exemption is removed. The dark theme is the sky: every dark token lives in the [data-surface="sky"] block and exists only inside an element that carries that attribute (#18). The one exempt pair, --on-sky-text-muted on --sky, is settled: disabled, non-interactive control labels only (#17, #18). Pairs come from the canvas boards Tokens, Foundations, Placement, Components and Motion and states. Not listed on purpose: --tertiary, --separator and --hairline (dividers and chevrons, decorative, never text), locked points (rgba white 28%, inactive), --lit-deep and --atmosphere (glow only).

pairs.why: inactive text only: labels of disabled, non-interactive controls, which WCAG 1.4.3 exempts; never for anything clickable (a tappable locked node is not exempt) or text meant to be read (user 2026-09-28, #17, #18)

star map line into the recommended star, tier 1, visible at rest on the nebula and star layers (#121)
pairs.why: The semantic-line 3:1 rule (WCAG 1.4.11) now holds for the tiers that are visible at rest and say how relevant a relation is now: tier 1 and tier 2. Over nebula haze it is checked in starmapContrast.test.ts (#121).

pairs.use: star map line from an in-progress star to its prerequisites, tier 2, visible at rest on the nebula layer (#121)
pairs.why: Gated with tier 1: the in-progress star's way back to what it needs is part of what to do now (#121).

pairs.use: star map line with both ends lit, tier 3, the path walked (#121)
pairs.why: Quiet on purpose (#121, #117 D1-D3: bright lines everywhere read as a tangle of scribbles). Both ends are already lit, which the stars' own glyphs show; nothing about it asks for action now. Only tiers 1 and 2 are held to the semantic-line 3:1.

pairs.use: star map line into a locked star, tier 4, dashed: only the lines of the star in focus (keyboard focus or chosen) or being dragged (#121, #138 D1); a relation across subjects at 70% of its tier's ink as a faint direction at the nebula band (#138 D2)
pairs.why: Darkest tier by design (#121), and since #138 D1 never drawn for every star: only around the one star in focus or in the hand (a locked star's card lists its missing prerequisites as links). Nothing on it can be done yet. Dashed, so about a third inked. Across subjects (#138 D2) the faint direction is never the only cue: the screen's edge names where it leads ("↘ Optics · Physics") in --on-sky-text-body on a patch of --sky, gated text above.

pairs.use: star map panorama: soft bridge between two related nebulae, and the glow between two galaxies that share prerequisites (#121)
pairs.why: Decoration at rest, almost dissolved in the star dust by decision (#121, #117 D1): the panorama shows no knowledge-point lines; a hovered or focused nebula brightens its bridges, and its relations are read out by its nebula link in the parallel DOM.

pairs.use: star map panorama: a galaxy's subject name, very faint and large under its stars, fading out as the zoom closes in (#137)
pairs.why: Decorative by decision (#123 round two A3: very faint, large, low contrast, so the galaxy reads as one whole without a label competing with its light). The same name is always the page heading and the subject switcher's segment, both gated text; the canvas name is never the only place it is said, and is not in the accessibility tree (#137).

pairs.use: star map panorama: the mathematics galaxy's name in its own colour, blue-violet, very faint and large under its stars, stepping back while one of its nebulae is hovered or focused (#143)
pairs.why: Decorative by decision, as --starmap-galaxy-name (#123 round two A3, #137): the same alpha, only tinted with its galaxy's base colour so a subject is told by hue (#142 round three A5, #143). The name is always the page heading and the subject switcher's segment, both gated text; the canvas name is not in the accessibility tree.
